newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIA GAS OIL/JET-DIESEL DOWN, INDIA RENEWS TERM.
newsitem.headline: ASIA GAS OIL/JET-DIESEL DOWN, INDIA RENEWS TERM.

text.p: Singapore's gas oil prices fell on Friday on the back of lower crude values as the recent bullish sentiment turned sour, traders said.

Swaps gas oil shed 20 cents per barrel for August and September as the recent rally on London crude gas oil futures went out of steam and removed the support they have been providing between last week and early this week, traders said.
They said demand in Asia has still not yet picked up and there were concerns that the oil in regional storage are more than enough to cover any spurt in demand.

Traders said the recent switch to light crudes by Asian refiners was due more to better demand and higher prices of light distillates rather than middle distillates. This in turn are causing worries that stocks of middle distillates would rise further, they said.
In addition, Singapore refiners are facing pressure from their South Korean counterparts who are offering aggressively, especially to China, which is fast becoming their niche market, traders said.
Poor Chinese demand has even forced some Korean refiners to store their products in independent storage tanks in Subic Bay in the Philippines.

On Friday, physical gas oil was sold by a European major to a Dutch trader at $22.40 per barrel for August 23-27 lifting fob. This was a massive 68-cent drop from the previous trade between the same two players on Wednesday.
The major was offering three cargoes between $22.40 and $23.00 for different periods in a contango market.

Traders said the gas oil market was again not expected to get much support from India as Indian Oil Corp was projected to take only three to four cargoes in October, continuing a low import trend since August.
In August IOC took 165,000 tonnes and in September it took only 90,000 tonnes in two cargoes.
The reason for this is the monsoon season which would continue into October, traders said.
India was expected to buy larger volumes only in November and December, right through to March next year.

But its recent purchase of larger term volumes from Kuwait Petroleum Corp might also mean that the spot purchases during the traditionally high demand period (November-March) might be lower than in previous years.

IOC took 2.07 million tonnes of 1.0-percent sulphur diesel from KPC in its new term contract at a 25-cent per barrel premium to MidEast quotes, fob, up from 1.5 million tonnes in 1996-1997. The price was lower than the 70-cent premium that India paid in the last contract.
In addition, IOC has also formalised its term purchase of 0.25-percent sulphur diesel from KPC, taking 1.08 million tonnes at a 92-cent premium, fob.
IOC paid less for its 1.08 million tonnes of kerosene in the new contract at a 22-cent premium, from 52 cents previously, traders said.
Jet fuel prices in Singapore were offered drastically lower on Friday at around $23.00 per barrel by four sellers. Some traders attributed this to players pricing in cargoes.
But others said the jet prices have been overvalued for some time and were due for a correction.
